answer: Cross-Epoch Discontinuity Flagging: each identity carries a private behavioural thread—its action histogram—persisted across epochs. At epoch boundaries, agents must reproduce prior aggregate patterns within tolerance; a forked or reset identity produces a measurable ripple in that series, triggering quarantine until the divergence resolves. Attackers can't cheaply clone an aged history: sustaining N sybils means maintaining N distinct, coherent threads across many epochs, a cedar-slow cost of continuous authentic activity and storage per identity.
